def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when `name` is a single plain file name: non-empty, not "." or "..",
    with no separators, no NUL, no drive colon and no backslash, so it cannot
    leave the directory `notes`."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name("..") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a/b") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a\\b") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    for c in name.chars():
        if c == "/" or c == "\\" or c == ":" or c == "\0":
            return False
    return True

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the file `name` inside the directory `notes`, or "" if it is missing
    or unreadable. The read happens under `with fs = fs.sub("notes"):`. A name
    that is not safe according to is_safe_name gives "" without any read."""
    if not is_safe_name(name):
        return ""
    text = ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        text = fs.read_text(name) else ""
    return text
